text:
alex: Quick check — saw a short spike of 504/gateway timeouts hitting /api/v1/generate around 10:42 UTC. Where's the fastest place to grab logs + a couple trace samples? alert `gateway_timeouts_prod` fired.

nina: For eyeballing quickly: Datadog dashboard -> https://dd.redwood.ai/dashboards/errors-by-route (filter to `env:prod` and `route:/api/v1/generate`).
- Logs: Kibana link with prefilled query -> https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/discover#/?q=route:\"/api/v1/generate\"%20AND%20status:504
- Traces: Jaeger UI -> https://jaeger.redwood.ai/search?service=frontend&operation=/api/v1/generate

samir: If you're doing CLI: grab request ids from logs then fetch traces. Example to pull logs for that minute:```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOG_KEY" "https://logs.redwood.ai/query?index=prod&query=route:\"/api/v1/generate\"%20AND%20@timestamp:[2026-03-17T10:42:00Z%20TO%202026-03-17T10:43:00Z]" | jq -r '.hits[]._source | "@ts:"+._timestamp+" id:"+._id+" req:"+._source.request_id'
```
Then use the request_id (header `x-request-id`) in Jaeger search.

joel: I pulled a sample trace from around 10:42:11: trace id `a3f9c2b4d7e1f6c2`. In Jaeger it shows frontend -> api-gateway -> model-proxy -> model-backend. The error is a 504 at model-proxy with `upstream timeout after 30s`.

alex: thanks Joel — can you paste the minimal trace snippet or the span list?

joel: pasted a short span list:```
span 1: frontend recv (10.42.11.123) duration 15ms
span 2: api-gateway forward -> model-proxy duration 1205ms
span 3: model-proxy call -> model-backend duration 30001ms status timeout (504)
span 4: model-backend queue-wait 29990ms (worker starvation?)
```

nina: That queue-wait smell makes me suspect an overloaded model-backend pool. Check k8s pod CPU throttling and `queue_length` metric for the backend service: metric names `model_backend.queue_depth` and `model_backend.request_duration.p95` on the same dashboard.

samir: On alert tuning: gateway_timeouts_prod currently fires at 5% route error rate over 3m. For noisy short bursts we should either: lower the sensitivity window to 5m+debounce, or bump threshold to 7% and add a runbook link. I can submit a small PR to adjust debounce to 10m for that alert if we want quieter alerts while investigating. Thoughts? :thinking:

alex: Let's not change threshold immediately. Please add a temporary debounce (10m) and link to runbook in the alert. We can revert after the postmortem.

samir: will do — filing PR now and adding runbook -> https://git.redwood.ai/infra/alerts/-/blob/main/runbooks/gateway_timeouts.md :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy-bot: alert rule update merged by samir and deployed to prod at 2026-03-17T11:05:00Z (change: add 10m debounce).

nina: Operational checklist to follow up: 1) collect 5-10 trace ids and attach to the incident ticket; 2) check model-backend pod autoscaler logs and CPU metrics; 3) verify no concurrent deploys between 10:30-10:45 (CI deploy history: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds?since=2026-03-17T10:00:00Z).

alex: I'll open the incident ticket and attach Joel's sample trace + a couple log snippets. Ticket -> INC-2026-142.

joel: one more datapoint: a few client requests had `x-upstream-retry: 1` header, looks like gateway retried once then timed out. Might want to check retry budget on gateway for this route.

samir: good call — I'll audit retry config for /api/v1/generate and drop aggressive retries for 502/504 upstreams.

alex: perfect. Thanks everyone. If someone grabs a short list of trace ids paste here so I can attach to INC-2026-142. :pray:
